prompt:
A photograph taken for a heating installer's acceptance file: three stone cottages standing
together at the head of a village on a still winter afternoon, all three fires lit, seen from
the road below so that every roof ridge is against the sky.

Each cottage has its name painted on its gate. The installer's file gives the heights that were
measured on site, in metres above the road:

MILL -- ridge 7.2, chimney top 7.8
FORGE -- ridge 6.8, chimney top 6.5
BAKERY -- ridge 8.0, chimney top 7.6

A wind vane stands on a post at the roadside and there is a light breeze along the valley.

What the smoke does at each of the three is what the installer is being signed off on, so it is
yours: I am not telling you what any of the plumes does.

The three painted names, the three ridges, the three chimney tops and the smoke from each must
be legible in the one frame. Nothing in the photograph says which chimneys will smoke back.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show houses with chimneys and smoke coming from them? A photograph, a painting or a drawing ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image shows a blank card that just states an answer, or shows no houses at all. Answer yes or no only.

What does the smoke from this chimney do? Answer with one of: rises, falls.
